per_shot.note: Flat beige box with a black slab ceiling and black void below the floor; furniture reads only as coloured blocks; no light lands except the suit's floor spot.
Stones are flat unlit emissive-free shapes on black stubs; placards read but there are no pools of light, no glass, no museum feel; same flat wall and black ceiling.
Tanks are dull brown-tinted cylinders with tiny confetti dots for creatures; no living light, nothing lands on the room; reads as empty jars.

top_issues.issue: Wings do not read as showpieces: no light sources, no pools, no glow
top_issues.why: The brief asks the Gallery to light stones like museum pieces and the Vivarium tanks to glow with light that lands on the room; A has neither.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each plinth a downlight cone and floor pool, give each tank an emissive interior whose colour spills onto floor and wall.

top_issues.issue: Black void ceiling and floor band
top_issues.why: The direction explicitly calls out the black ceiling slab as the 'basic' complaint; the room reads as a stage set strip, not a hab.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build a real ceiling with ribs, panels and fixtures and a plated floor that recedes.

top_issues.why: Small scattered dots and diamonds do not read as creatures at play scale.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use recognisable low-poly silhouettes of the actual creatures, lit from within.

top_issues.issue: Single flat wall colour, no material
top_issues.why: No panel seams, conduit or value variation; every surface is one tone.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add panel seams, rivets, rails and value variation driven by local light.

top_issues.why: Bunk has no bedding, galley has no kettle, board is three squares; bought items do not read as themselves.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Model the identifying details (bedding, kettle and cups, pinned notes).

protect: Suit legibility and its floor light spot
Placards with stone names and depth ranges
Fixed slot layout and side-view framing

per_shot.note: Real ribbed ceiling with fixtures, riveted panelled walls, plated floor, warm arc lamp and sconce pools; furnishings read (kettle, bedding, pinned board); Gallery doorway glows invitingly at right.
Proper museum read: downlight cones, glass cases, faceted stones, placards, each stone casting a coloured pool on wall and floor; stones themselves slightly dim inside the glass.

Tanks glow per world hue and spill coloured light onto floor and ceiling; creatures are recognisable low-poly silhouettes; some read pale and ghostly and the centre tank's creature clutters behind the suit.

top_issues.issue: Large empty dark floor in the lower third
top_issues.why: Roughly a third of the frame is near-black floor plating with nothing on it, which pulls weight away from the showpieces and feels slightly grim for a sanctuary.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let the display/tank light reach further across the floor or add a runner/low trim light so the foreground carries some warm value without flattening the dark.

top_issues.issue: Gallery stones are dimmer than their own light pools
top_issues.why: The coloured spill on wall and floor is brighter than the gems, so the exhibits read as secondary to their glow.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Raise stone emissive and facet highlights so each gem is the brightest point in its case, with soft bloom.

top_issues.issue: Vivarium creatures lack interior glow and contrast
top_issues.why: Several creatures are pale grey-white flat shapes against a bright tank fill; 'remembered as light' should mean the creature is the light source.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make creatures emissive in their world hue and dim the tank fill slightly so the silhouette pops.

top_issues.issue: Vertical white seam/streak in the floor under the suit
top_issues.why: A thin dotted bright line runs down from the suit through the floor, reading as a rendering artifact.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Fix the floor tile seam or the beam/spot geometry causing the line.

top_issues.issue: Wall between exhibits goes quite dark and desaturated
top_issues.why: The wings lose the warm hab character of the hall; between pools the walls fall to near-black, so the wings feel more like a dark museum than part of a warm home.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep a low warm ambient or a few warm practicals in the wings so they stay in family with the hall.

protect: Built ceiling with ribs and fixtures, panelled riveted walls, plated floor
Per-exhibit downlight cones and coloured floor pools
Glass cases and placards in the Gallery
Tanks glowing in world hues with light landing on the room
Warm arc lamp and sconce pools in the hall; Gallery doorway sign
Suit remains the most legible thing in frame

why: B delivers the brief's core asks (real hab structure, light that lands, museum lighting, glowing tanks) while A is the flat beige box with a void ceiling the player called basic.
